s1.syndrome_frame: A slowly enlarging, firm, painless mass in the left labia majora with a long history of recurrence
salient_findings: Slowly enlarging mass in the left labia majora over 10 years
Mass is firm, painless, and immobile
History of multiple recurrences after excision
Imaging shows a heterogeneous, hypervascular subcutaneous mass
key_facts: 64-year-old woman
Mass in the left labia majora
Mass is approximately 7 × 4 cm
Normal vital signs
Normal routine laboratory tests
History of excised mass in the Bartholin’s gland
Histopathology showed chondroid syringoma
Recurrence in the labia majora with histology showing clear cell hidradenoma
Ultrasound showed a 4.2 × 8 cm heterogeneous, hypervascular subcutaneous mass
CT scan demonstrated a 3.8 × 7.2 cm heterogeneous, contrast-enhancing lesion
Low-density focus in the liver suggestive of a simple cyst
Vulvar mass was excised and reported as chondroid syringoma
Recurrence near the fourchette three months after excision

raw.rationale: The patient's mass was repeatedly reported as chondroid syringoma after excision and histopathologic evaluation, indicating a strong evidence-based reason for this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Clear cell hidradenoma
rejected.why: Although the patient had a history of clear cell hidradenoma, the most recent and repeated histopathology reports indicated chondroid syringoma.

rejected.label: Aggressive angiomyxoma
rejected.why: There is no mention of the characteristic aggressive behavior or angiomyxoma histology in the patient's history or laboratory results.

rejected.label: Bartholin gland carcinoma
rejected.why: The patient's history of excised mass in the Bartholin’s gland showed chondroid syringoma, not carcinoma, and there is no indication of malignant behavior in the provided information.

rejected.label: Desmoid tumor
rejected.why: There is no mention of the characteristic desmoid tumor histology or behavior in the patient's history or laboratory results.
